initial_prompt: Write me a poem about the feeling of almost remembering something.

messages.content: Write me a poem about the feeling of almost remembering something.

# At the Edge of Knowing

There's a word for this—
I almost have it,
a shape my tongue remembers
but my mind won't hold.

Like reaching through water
for a stone I can see
perfectly clearly
until my hand arrives.

Something about a kitchen,
late afternoon light,
someone was singing—
or was that a different life?

The feeling has texture:
velvet worn thin,
a door half-open
to a room I've never entered
but somehow recognize.

My brain sends scouts
to the borders of itself,
returns with rumors,
the scent of something burning,
a name beginning with—

It was important once.
Or it will be.
The past tense of a thing
I haven't lost yet.

I stand at the window
of my own remembering,
fog on the glass,
tracing letters backward,
waiting for the clearing
that may never come—

and still, somehow,
*almost* is its own
country. I live there
more than I'd admit.
